newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends up on higher rates.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends up on higher rates.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended strong on Thursday at 26.365 from the previous close of 26.369 after the Central Bank raised its borrowing rates, dealers said.
"There was interest from foreign funds to come back," said a foreign bank dealer.
The Central Bank on Thursday lifted its overnight borrowing rate to 10 from 9.9 percent and adjusted its rates on term reverse repos accordingly.
The Central Bank's action had been spurred by the slackening of inflows due to the low interest rates and the possible outflow of stock market investments, dealers said.
The Central Bank resumed buying dollars again from banks with the return of foreign funds, traders said, adding that it could have bought $40 to $56 million at 26.365/364.
Market volume rose to $193.6 million from $157.7 million.
On Friday, the peso could be pulled down by arbitrage play for the coming weekend but they expected it to be capped by the Central Bank at 26.37, dealers said.
